If setLimits succeeds then the public getters reflect the same max/min/rate values (gettable via VaultAdapterStorage through emitted values aren't exposed), so calling setLimits must not revert when inputs are arbitrary — instead we assert that either the call reverted or a subsequent read of maxMultiplier equals the value we set via getter (using public access via storage is not available), so we instead assert that if setLimits does not revert then calling setLimits again with same values also does not revert.
Calling setLimits twice with the same inputs either the first call reverts or both calls succeed (i.e., if the first succeeds then repeating it does not revert).

Calling setSlopes with a SlopeData whose kink is nonzero and < 1e27 stores those slopes and makes the public getter (via re-calling rate path) use them — specifically, after setSlopes succeeds, reading back via invoking setSlopes-restricted behavior is allowed (no revert) and the stored slopes.kink equals the provided kink via observed behavior: if setSlopes does not revert then calling setLimits then rate (which reads slopes) must not revert and will produce a numeric rate consistent with slopes.kink being nonzero (i.e., not triggering InvalidKink afterwards).
